flagged.evidence: The page says “the cusp and jump counterexamples use the ACL and change-of-variables interfaces that declare the Axiom of Choice”. The current cusp item assumes Countable Choice and computes classical weak derivatives, interior integrals and arc lengths without invoking ACL. Its cited thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure explicitly says “assume the Axiom of Countable Choice”; the general C1 change-of-variables supplier also assumes Countable Choice. The jump item carries AC through the sharp trace theorem. The collective attribution therefore misstates both the cusp proof and the change-of-variables hypotheses.

The Source notes say “Hajlasz and Martio (printed pp. 221-222) record the failure of a bounded linear right inverse at p=1”. Those pages introduce the trace problem and the p>1 theory; the Peetre attribution occurs in Remarks after Theorem 10, part (4), printed p. 243. This is confirmed by the complete endpoint paragraph in the [cited PDF](https://sites.pitt.edu/~hajlasz/OriginalPublications/HajlaszM-Traces-JFunctAnal-143-1997-221-246.pdf) and agrees with this item's corrected frontmatter locator. The body still gives the wrong location.
